But not many people bonsai avocados, should I be trimming it now? Should I cut the stem, any tips or advice here?

Typically potential bonsai are planted in the ground for a period (a year or more) to let the trunk grow thick. I'm sure a large pot will suffice as well if you have the time to let it grow. As it grows you can bend and wire the trunk into whatever shape you want. Once it has grown enough, the tree is pruned back.

I'm not sure how to tackle pruning your avocado since it is so tall. I don't think it will survive if you prune it below the lowest node which looks to be near the top at the leaves. The tree will grow two new shoots at the node below the pruning cut, which you can use to force branching. But if the lowest node is up high then the trunk will forever be branchless.

Another neat technique is to periodically raise the tree a little further out of the ground and put the (toughened, bark covered) roots over a rock, for example. That may help make the trunk more interesting if you keep it branch free.

You might need to get creative with the trunk shape or take cuttings to make bonsai from. If you root a cutting you have more control over where the nodes are and more flexibility to create branches closer to the ground.

Root a cutting means to cut off a branch or growing tip of the plant and coax it into developing roots of its own. It's also called cloning. Often rooting hormones are used to speed up root development before the cutting withers or rots.

You want it this height but without the long exposed trunk right? With branches and leaves between its currently lowest leaf and the ground? It doesn't look like that's possible since it grew so tall without making a node (a lump in the stem where leaves or branches stick out from). You can see better than I, though.

I wouldn't suggest cutting anything just yet because it looks like there are only 2 or 3 nodes so far. I would probably start by gently and slowly bending the trunk (and wiring it so it stays) into an interesting shape. Probably trying a shape which brings the leaves closer to the ground, like a sideways S. If you shorten the trunk the tree can grow more bush on the top for you to shape while not getting taller.

Bonsai is kind of aggravating because you can't make the tree do just anything, you have to work with how it grows. If there aren't nodes on the trunk right now, you can't force the tree to grow leaves on the trunk.
